about: The small coercions that turn a panel's JSON into catalogue fields.
notes: Arguments are the coercion's name and the raw value, so one suite covers all of them.

`str`, `toInt` and `num` treat an empty string as absent, not as zero. Panels send "" for a missing number constantly, and an implementation reading that as 0 fills a catalogue with channel number zero and a rating of nought without failing anywhere.

`catchupDays` is the only one with a judgement in it: panels disagree about whether the flag or the duration says there is an archive, so a duration alone is believed and a flag alone is taken as one day — erring towards asking the provider rather than hiding a feature the account has paid for.

cases.name: str keeps a string
str stringifies a number
cases.why: Panels send stream_id as a number on some endpoints and a string on others; the id must come out the same either way or the two syncs disagree about which channel is which.

cases.name: str treats an empty string as absent
str treats null as absent
str keeps zero, which is a real id
toInt reads a numeric string
toInt keeps a number
toInt treats an empty string as absent, not as zero
toInt treats a non-number as absent
toInt truncates rather than rounding
toInt reads a leading number
cases.why: parseInt stops at the first non-digit. Recorded because it is a real difference from a strict parse: a second implementation refusing this would drop channel numbers that currently work.

cases.name: toInt keeps zero
num reads a decimal
num treats an empty string as absent
num refuses a number with text after it
cases.why: Unlike toInt. The difference is deliberate: a rating is either a number or it is missing, and half-reading one invents a score.

cases.name: num keeps zero
num treats null as absent
text trims
text treats whitespace alone as absent
text stringifies a number
text treats anything else as absent
text treats an object as absent rather than stringifying it
cases.why: Otherwise a plot reads `[object Object]`, which is worse than an empty one because it looks like data.

cases.name: firstImage takes the first of an array
firstImage accepts a bare string
cases.why: backdrop_path is an array on most panels and a single string on some.

cases.name: firstImage of an empty array is absent
firstImage does not look past an empty first entry
cases.why: A limitation, recorded rather than endorsed: a panel sending an empty string before a real URL loses the image. Harmless enough that changing it is not worth the risk of changing what a catalogue looks like, but a second implementation must match it, or the two disagree about which films have artwork.

cases.name: parseDuration reads hours, minutes and seconds
parseDuration reads minutes and seconds
parseDuration refuses a bare number
cases.why: `90` could be minutes or seconds and guessing wrong puts the seek bar an hour out.

cases.name: parseDuration refuses text
parseDuration of nothing is nothing
catchupDays believes a duration on its own
catchupDays takes a flag on its own as one day
catchupDays prefers the duration when both are set
catchupDays of neither is no archive
catchupDays reads them as strings too
catchupDays of an empty row is no archive
